pr_title: Keep M01/M02 local gates honest with usecase boundary
summary: F4 operator/contributor UX review for PR #8: the gate surface is mostly understandable and checked, but transitional naming aliases and runbook drift make the contributor path ambiguous. Highest severity MAJOR.

findings.issue: The architecture-boundaries gate still accepts both corrected roles (`usecase`, `app`) and legacy/transitional roles (`application`, `runtime`, `api`, `worker`, `test`) without an operator-visible sunset condition. New contributors can pass the gate while copying old layer names, then later be surprised by follow-up cleanup or stricter doctrine.
findings.remediation: Add a ratchet fixture or date/phase-scoped allowlist that names the exact legacy role records still tolerated and prints a warning/remediation path before the aliases become hard failures.

findings.file: docs/runbooks/sanctioned-primitives/preflight.md as touched by PR #8 before ADR-0116 retirement
findings.issue: PR #8 adjusted gate honesty while operator runbooks were still in transition around sanctioned primitives. Even though later PR #10 retired the external-tool wording, the PR #8 contributor journey still mixed local gate commands with stale coordination-tool expectations.
findings.remediation: For each gate-hardening PR, require a matching runbook/CLI help check showing the exact current command sequence and explicitly marking retired tools as tombstones, not prerequisites.
